newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada savings bond sales rise 24 percent.
newsitem.headline: Canada savings bond sales rise 24 percent.

text.p: Sales of 1996 Canada Savings Bonds rose to C$5.7 billion, 24 percent above last year's level, Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Monday.

"After redemptions the sales were in fact 38 percent higher than last year," Martin told Parliament, adding that this reflected partially the "innovative 10-year guaranteed minimum pricing structure."

"For those who might not have had a chance to buy the Canada Savings Bonds and who would like to do, the government will be introducing a new retirement savings product, to be launched in February in time for the RRSP season," he said.
RRSPs, registered retirement savings plans, are designed to defer some taxes until after retirement. The deadline for contributing for the 1996 tax year is the end of February 1997.
